lean.statement:
theorem result
    {W H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (μ ν : Measure W) (feature : W → H) (label : H)
    (hμ : Integrable feature μ) (hν : Integrable feature ν) :
    let m : H := ∫ w, feature w ∂μ
    let n : H := ∫ w, feature w ∂ν
    let potential : W → ℝ := fun w => 2 * ⟪m - label, feature w⟫_ℝ
    Integrable potential μ ∧ Integrable potential ν ∧
    ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ) =
      2 * ⟪m - label, n - m⟫_ℝ) ∧
    (‖n - label‖ ^ 2 - ‖m - label‖ ^ 2 -
      ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) = ‖n - m‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (‖m - label‖ ^ 2 + ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) ≤
      ‖n - label‖ ^ 2) ∧
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => ‖m + t • (n - m) - label‖ ^ 2)
      ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) 0
approved_definition_context: Integrable means genuine Bochner integrability, including almost-everywhere strong measurability; it is not a finite value of a totalized nonintegrable integral.
The two vector integrals are literal and unnormalized; the scalar subtraction is a difference of real integrals. The derivative parameter varies in the displayed affine vector-space curve.
